dedupe_keys.name: openfoam open source cfd used for wind flow around buildings

description: OpenFOAM is free, open-source computational fluid dynamics software developed mainly by OpenCFD Ltd since 2004, now within Keysight. It solves problems from complex flows with chemical reactions, turbulence and heat transfer to acoustics, solid mechanics and electromagnetics, and has a large commercial and academic user base. OpenCFD releases a version every six months, in June and December, after several hundred daily unit tests, weekly test batteries and a large industrial test set before each release; the latest listed release is from 26 June 2026. OpenCFD transferred the rights to versions after 8 August 2011 to the OpenFOAM Foundation, which also issues releases. Coverage: generic. Access: free downloads for Linux, macOS and Windows and source code, with paid training and support. Licence: open source. Caveats: building wind studies need careful meshing, turbulence model choice and validation. Simulation uses: wind loads and pedestrian wind comfort around buildings, natural ventilation and pollutant dispersion. Related records: ENVI-met and FDS.
